newsitem.title: ROMANIA: St Andrew relics draw Romanian crowds, politicians.
newsitem.headline: St Andrew relics draw Romanian crowds, politicians.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Romanian Orthodox faithful and politicians campaigning for next month's elections streamed to northeastern city of Iasi on Monday on a pilgrimage to remains believed to be those of St Andrew.
Thousands of worshippers queued for hours at Iasi cathedral to touch a silver casket with relics of Andrew, who is said to have spread the gospel among ancient Romanians 2,000 years ago.

Romanian Orthodox Church leaders had the relics flown in from Patras shrine in Greece to Iasi at the weekend to launch week-long ceremonies marking a local saint's day. But the religious occasion took on a strongly political feel.
On Sunday, Romanian state television showed left-wing President Ion Iliescu bowing to kiss the relics at the end of a religious service at the cathedral.
Iliescu is completing a tour of northeast Romania, once his electoral stronghold, on his campaign for November 3 polls.

On Monday, seven of Iliescu's challengers, including his two main rivals, opposition Democratic Convention bloc leader Emil Constantinescu and ex-Prime Minister Petre Roman, took turns to visit Andrew's relics. But many pilgrims who thronged the area around the cathedral, eager to pray for good health or relief at the relics, were sceptical about the presence of party leaders.
"Politicians have nothing to do here, they shouldn't turn these ceremonies into electoral propaganda," one woman said.

Police cordons struggled to keep the crowds under control, as religious fervour gripped the city. According to local police estimates, up to 300,000 pilgrims, roughly the equivalent of the city's entire population, had flocked to Iasi by Monday.
"I have been waiting for 14 hours for a chance to touch the relics and pray. I am lonely and ill and I know the relics can work wonders," pensioner Elena Vuta, 53, said.
A skull said to be that of Andrew was displayed in a silver casket before thousands of worshippers outside Iasi cathedral, along with relics of the city's patron saint Paraschiva.
Andrew, one of the 12 Apostles whom Christ sent to preach the gospel, is believed to have travelled northward, across what is now Romania's Black Sea coast, around the year A.D. 70.
Official census data show that more than 86 percent of Romanians belong to the mainstream Orthodox church, which has a centuries-old tradition of cooperation with state authorities.
